ui.claudeDesktopBundleDescription: Install the NodeTool extension bundled with this app. Claude Desktop opens its install dialog; confirm it there.

menus.streamableHTTPWithSSEAsTheFallback: Streamable HTTP, with SSE as the fallback.
menus.pmSubIncluded: Packs that ship with NodeTool. Turn a pack off to hide its nodes. A pack toggle takes effect after the server restarts. Provider nodes appear when you add their API key.
menus.pmSubPython: Node packs from PyPI that run in the Python worker. The server restarts after you install, update or uninstall a pack.
menus.pmSubThirdparty: Third-party packs run in-process as the server user. Only trust packs you know.
menus.pmSubRuntimes: Programs that run on this computer: local AI engines such as llama.cpp and stable-diffusion.cpp, media tools such as FFmpeg, and languages. Local models and some nodes need them.
menus.customApiKeyHelper: The URL and key are encrypted and stored per account. The same values can come from the environment instead, as CUSTOM_{{slug}}_BASE_URL and CUSTOM_{{slug}}_API_KEY.
menus.removeEndpointBody: Remove {{name}}? Workflows that reference its models stop resolving.
menus.externalServersCaption: Give the agent the tools of any MCP server: Blender, Hugging Face, or a script of your own. Works with every model provider.
menus.removeServerBody: Remove {{name}}? Its tools leave the agent's toolbelt.
menus.agentAccessIntro: Point Claude Code, Claude Desktop, or any MCP client at this server over HTTP. Create a token below and paste the configuration it produces.
menus.mcpNotServed: This server does not serve {{code}}. Set {{flag}}=1 in its environment and restart it.
menus.noAuthModeNotice: This server checks no credential — it trusts its own network. A token still works and is the safer choice if you reach it from anywhere but this machine.
menus.revokeClientBody: {{client}} will no longer be able to reach this server. It will need to reconnect and be approved again.
menus.noFolderSettings: No folder settings available or defined in the 'Folders' group.
menus.mcpIntroLead: Use NodeTool from Claude Code, Codex, or OpenCode through the
menus.mcpIntroTail: . The agent gets NodeTool workflows, media generation, assets, nodes, and collections as tools.

app-assistant.title: Build a mini app
app-assistant.result: The app displays a completed answer and its input/output widgets remain bound.
app-assistant.startingState: The Examples page with the mini-app gallery ready to browse.
app-assistant.task: Open a mini app, provide its input, and run it once from the app surface.
app-assistant.description: Describe an app in a sentence — an input, a button, an answer — and the assistant binds the workflow as an operation and places each widget against something the app declares.
app-assistant.learn0: Turning a workflow into an app anyone can run
app-assistant.learn1: Saving a value as a setting that persists between sessions
app-assistant.learn2: Binding widgets to inputs, outputs, and variables

ask-ai.title: Ask the AI
ask-ai.result: The answer streams into the output and remains available to the next node.
ask-ai.startingState: A new workflow canvas with an empty input and output path.
ask-ai.tagline: A question in, a streamed answer out
ask-ai.task: Connect a question input to an LLM node, ask for a short API explanation, and run it.
ask-ai.description: The simplest chat-style graph: type a question, send it to an LLM node, and watch the answer stream in phrase by phrase before it lands in a Preview.
ask-ai.learn0: Feeding a question into an LLM node
ask-ai.learn1: Watching an answer stream as it generates

chat-agent-qa.title: Ask the chat agent
chat-agent-qa.result: The chat shows a web-search tool call followed by a streamed answer.
chat-agent-qa.startingState: A new Global Chat conversation with an empty composer.
chat-agent-qa.tagline: Global Chat · tool calls, streamed live
chat-agent-qa.task: Ask a current-facts question that requires a web search.
chat-agent-qa.description: A question goes straight to Global Chat: the agent calls a web-search tool in the open, then streams its answer back token by token.
chat-agent-qa.learn0: Sending a message from Global Chat
chat-agent-qa.learn1: Watching a tool call run in the open
chat-agent-qa.learn2: Reading a streamed answer as it arrives

combine-inputs.title: Combine two inputs
combine-inputs.result: Preview shows the completed template with both input values substituted.
combine-inputs.startingState: A new workflow canvas with two text inputs ready to connect.
combine-inputs.task: Connect name and topic inputs to a template prompt, fill both values, and run it.
combine-inputs.description: The first graph that branches in: two text inputs flow into one Prompt node that fills a template, composing a single result from reusable parts.
combine-inputs.learn0: Wiring several inputs into one node

connect-run.title: Connect & run
connect-run.result: Preview shows HELLO NODETOOL and each connected node reports completion.
connect-run.startingState: A new workflow canvas ready for a small connected graph.
connect-run.tagline: Follow a connected graph from input to output
connect-run.task: Connect a text input to Uppercase and then to Preview, run it with hello nodetool, and inspect the output.
connect-run.description: Trace the existing connections from a text input through Uppercase, watch the nodes execute, and read HELLO NODETOOL in Preview.
connect-run.learn0: Inputs, outputs, and how handles connect
connect-run.learn1: Running a graph and watching nodes complete
connect-run.learn2: Finding a node's result in a Preview

describe-image.title: Describe an image
describe-image.result: The vision response describes the image and is available in the downstream output.
describe-image.startingState: A new workflow canvas with an image input ready to fill.
describe-image.tagline: Show the AI a picture, get words back
describe-image.task: Add an image, connect it to an Agent, and run the graph to describe what is visible.
describe-image.description: The first multimodal graph: drop a picture into an Image Input, wire it into an Agent, and watch the model look at the image and describe it in words.
describe-image.learn0: Bringing an image into a graph
describe-image.learn1: Sending a picture to a vision model

first-workflow.title: Build your first workflow
first-workflow.result: The graph completes and the generated image appears on the canvas.
first-workflow.startingState: A new workflow in the guided workflow setup.
first-workflow.tagline: Text → enhance → image, end to end
first-workflow.task: Build a text-to-image graph with a text input, an enhancement step, and an image generator, then run it.
first-workflow.description: Watch a complete AI pipeline run on the canvas: a prompt is enhanced by an LLM, then turned into an image — all from connected nodes, no code.
first-workflow.learn0: How nodes pass data through their handles
first-workflow.learn1: Reading live status: running rings, streaming text, progress
first-workflow.learn2: Where generated outputs appear on the canvas

jsscript-assistant.title: Write a JS script
jsscript-assistant.tagline: JS scripts · ports, body, saved test
jsscript-assistant.description: Say what goes in and what should come out. The assistant declares the ports first, writes the body, and saves a test case that grades it in the sandbox.
jsscript-assistant.learn0: Declaring ports as the script's contract
jsscript-assistant.learn1: Reading a body that runs sandboxed — no filesystem access
jsscript-assistant.learn2: Keeping a saved case that catches the next breaking edit

jsscript-repair.title: A test catches it
jsscript-repair.tagline: JS scripts · red, then the repair, then green
jsscript-repair.description: Name the edge case you do not trust. The assistant saves it as a test, runs it red with the reason in the open, repairs the body, and runs the same cases green.
jsscript-repair.learn0: Asking for the check before asking for the fix
jsscript-repair.learn1: Reading a failing run instead of a summary of one
jsscript-repair.learn2: Keeping the case saved so the next edit fails here first

list-generator.title: Generate a list
list-generator.result: The output contains multiple list items that can be passed to a downstream node.
list-generator.startingState: A new workflow canvas with no nodes connected.
list-generator.task: Connect a topic input to a list-generating LLM node and run it for weekend trip ideas.
list-generator.description: Turn a single topic into a structured list with one LLM node, then feed it downstream. The pattern behind batching, looping, and bulk generation.
list-generator.learn0: Driving an LLM node from an input
list-generator.learn1: Streaming multi-item output as it arrives
list-generator.learn2: Passing a list into the rest of a workflow

script-assistant.title: Write and voice a script
script-assistant.result: The script contains cast speakers, written lines, and an audio take for each speaker.
script-assistant.startingState: A new script with no cast or dialogue.
script-assistant.task: Ask the assistant for a short two-speaker script, then have it voice the lines.
script-assistant.description: From a blank page to voiced audio in one ask: the assistant casts the speakers, writes their lines, then synthesizes a take for each one.
script-assistant.learn0: Describing a script by length, voices, and tone
script-assistant.learn1: How speakers are cast before any line is written
script-assistant.learn2: Voicing lines into takes you can swap or re-record

sketch-assistant.title: Edit a sketch by asking
sketch-assistant.result: The wash layer appears in the layer panel with the requested blend mode and opacity.
sketch-assistant.startingState: A new sketch with a blank layer stack.
sketch-assistant.tagline: Sketch editor · the assistant paints the layer
sketch-assistant.task: Ask the assistant to add a soft wash layer and set its blend mode and opacity.
sketch-assistant.description: Say what you want changed and the assistant works the real layer tools: it adds the layer, sets the blend mode, and dials in opacity while you watch the panel update.
sketch-assistant.learn0: Asking for an edit against the layer stack you already have
sketch-assistant.learn1: Watching layers appear in the panel as the assistant works
sketch-assistant.learn2: Taking over by hand — every edit stays yours to change

sketch-correction.title: Correct it without starting over
sketch-correction.result: The existing layer is amended in place and the layer count stays unchanged.
sketch-correction.startingState: A new sketch ready for an assistant-led edit.
sketch-correction.tagline: Sketch editor · the second ask amends the first
sketch-correction.task: Make one assistant edit, then ask it to reduce the effect without creating another layer.
sketch-correction.description: The wash comes back too strong. Saying so in the next message edits the layer that is already there — the stack stays the same size and nothing is regenerated.
sketch-correction.learn0: Correcting a result instead of starting the ask again
sketch-correction.learn1: Reading which tool call the correction actually ran
sketch-correction.learn2: Taking the last step yourself with the panel controls

storyboard-ask.title: It asks before it spends
storyboard-ask.result: The assistant waits before spending, then creates the clarified shot list after your answer.
storyboard-ask.startingState: A new storyboard with no shots and no render started.
storyboard-ask.tagline: Storyboard · a question, not a guess
storyboard-ask.task: Give the assistant an incomplete brief, answer its follow-up question, and approve the board.
storyboard-ask.description: An under-specified brief gets a question back. The board stays empty and nothing renders while you decide, then your answer picks the format and the shot count.
storyboard-ask.learn0: Why an ambiguous brief comes back as a question
storyboard-ask.learn1: What the assistant does while it waits on you: nothing
storyboard-ask.learn2: Approving the spend once the shots read right

storyboard-assistant.title: Board a shot list
storyboard-assistant.result: The board contains an approved shot list with a rendered still for each shot.
storyboard-assistant.startingState: A new storyboard with an empty shot list.
storyboard-assistant.task: Describe a short piece, review the generated shot list, and approve it for rendering.
storyboard-assistant.description: Describe the piece and the assistant writes the shots — camera and all — before spending a frame. Approve the board, then the stills render shot by shot.
storyboard-assistant.learn0: Getting a shot list before any image is generated
storyboard-assistant.learn1: Revising a shot while it is still free to change
storyboard-assistant.learn2: Rendering stills across the board in one call

summarize-text.title: Summarize a document
summarize-text.result: Preview contains a shorter set of key points while the source remains available for comparison.
summarize-text.startingState: A new workflow canvas with an empty text path.
summarize-text.tagline: Long text in, key points out
summarize-text.task: Feed a long passage into a Summarizer node, run it, and send the summary to Preview.
summarize-text.description: Condense an article, transcript, or any block of text into a short summary with a single Summarizer node, streaming it as it writes.
summarize-text.learn0: Feeding a long passage into a Summarizer node
summarize-text.learn1: Watching the summary stream as it generates
summarize-text.learn2: Passing the result into the rest of a workflow

timeline-trim-arrange.title: Cut a scene together
timeline-trim-arrange.result: The timeline plays the arranged cut with the caption aligned to the dialogue.
timeline-trim-arrange.startingState: A new timeline with empty tracks and no clips.
timeline-trim-arrange.task: Place two clips, trim their cut, add a caption, and preview the finished sequence.
timeline-trim-arrange.description: Watch the opening clip shorten, the next shot meet its edge, and a caption appear on its track. Then preview the finished cut.
timeline-trim-arrange.learn0: Trimming and arranging clips on tracks
timeline-trim-arrange.learn2: Scrubbing and previewing the cut live

jsScript.agentsReadHelper: Agents read this to decide whether to call the script.
